Product overview

This range covers everything that holds, chills or clears away: tabletop 1 L buckets, classic 4 L and 8 L champagne buckets, a 12 L double-wall cooler for bottle service, and a boat-shaped 5 L bucket built for seafood and grazing displays. The LED versions add rechargeable illumination for bottle service and evening terrace service, and the wine tasting spittoon buckets give tasting rooms a hygienic, purpose-built solution for guided flights.

The LED Ice Bucket 4 L with Charger (model YJ314) holds 4 L and is moulded in PS and ABS with LED. Polystyrene gives the clearest glass look at the lowest unit cost. Hand washing, or a top-rack rinse, keeps the surface clearest for longest. Unit weight is 650 g and it is packed 10 pcs / 44x31x46 cm / 9 kg, so you can plan freight per carton rather than per unit.

Because the tooling is ours, rim thickness, base weight and box counts stay consistent between orders — the single most common complaint buyers raise about sourcing drinkware from trading companies. Every run is checked against the approved pre-production sample before it is packed.

This item can be produced in your own colour and decorated with your logo, event name or a client's brand. Retail-ready colour boxes, hang tags and UPC barcodes are available for retail and e-commerce programmes. Add it to a mixed order and we will consolidate it with the rest of your items so it ships as one entry.

Six checks before you release a branded order

  1. Start from a dated sample. Record the model, body colour, surface finish, controls and every included item against it. A product photo is not an order specification.
  2. Approve battery and charging as one system. The battery format, charging input, connector and cable are confirmed together against the current version, not assumed from a catalogue field.
  3. Define your cork and bottle range. State the corks and bottles the unit must handle, and approve an observable test on the sample. We do not publish performance claims the sample has not demonstrated.
  4. Approve the gift or retail presentation. Neutral box, colour box, gift insert, barcode, manual language and importer information — the exact presentation affects the price and the inspection standard.
  5. Keep artwork claims evidence-based. Logo, colour and layout are yours to decide; box and manual text must match the approved sample, and claims the record does not support are excluded.
  6. Inspect the final version. Model identity, colour, finish, operating and release sequence, accessories, labels, box and carton count — checked against the approved revision, not against a generic unit.

The destination market changes what the approval file must carry: operator and importer information, language, labelling, and the documentation route for battery shipments. We build that file with you order by order. Import duty, taxes and clearance remain the responsibility of the importer of record.
